# Results — Study 864 (Yield-Curve Twist / Butterfly)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: beyond the
curve's **level** and **slope**, its **curvature** — the butterfly `fly = 2·y10 − y5 − y30`
(the belly vs the wings) and its change `dfly` (a "twist") — predicts forward Treasury (IEF/TLT)
and equity (SPY) returns, distinct from the 2s10s slope (studies 66/132) and the roll-down carry
(study 380). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month
is dropped) — the sample is sliced as-of 2026-06-30. Fingerprint `5136638af800` (IEF_close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return): **^FVX** (5y yield), **^TNX** (10y yield), **^TYX** (30y yield), **IEF** (7-10y UST), **TLT** (20+y UST), **SPY** (S&P 500), **2002-07-31 → 2026-06-30**, **6,011** trading days |
| Signal | **butterfly** `fly = 2·y10 − y5 − y30` (curvature, %-points) and its change `dfly` (the *twist*); rolling-252d z-scored, **lagged one day** (known at close `t−1`) |
| Target | forward **log return** of IEF (primary — the belly ETF), TLT and SPY over `h ∈ {5, 21, 63}` business days (close `t` → close `t+h`) |
| Controls (dedup) | the **5s10s slope** `y10 − y5` and the **level** `y10`, z-scored the same way — the joint regression asks whether curvature adds *incrementally* |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → position/return from close `t`. The costed timer charges a one-way cost per switch on the traded NAV |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, Bartlett, lag = horizon) *t* on the regression loading and the Q5−Q1 spread; a 500-permutation placebo; a three-era robustness cut; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |
| Survivorship | **none** — index/ETF total-return series, no cross-section. Named on the Signal axis for completeness |

## The headline — forward return ~ lagged z(butterfly), HAC *t*

| target | horizon | β (bps / +1σ fly) | HAC *t* | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **IEF** | 5d | +3.6 | **+2.13** | 0.31% |
| **IEF** | **21d** | **+16.9** | **+2.34** | **1.58%** |
| **IEF** | 63d | +46.8 | **+2.42** | 4.04% |
| TLT | 21d | +16.1 | +1.12 | 0.35% |
| SPY | 21d | −24.7 | −1.60 | 0.57% |

The butterfly **does** load on forward **IEF** (belly) returns with the economically sensible
**positive** sign — a *cheap belly* (high `fly`, the 10y yield high relative to the 5y/30y wings)
precedes the belly ETF *rising* (its yield mean-reverting down) — and the full-sample HAC *t*
nudges just past 2 at every horizon (**+2.13 / +2.34 / +2.42**). It is much weaker on the long
bond **TLT** (*t* = +1.12; the 30y wing is *in* the butterfly, so TLT is a poor belly proxy) and
insignificantly **negative** on **SPY** (*t* = −1.60). So the effect, such as it is, is a
**belly-Treasury** story.

## Incremental — is the butterfly just repackaged slope? (the dedup test)

Joint regression, forward IEF `h=21` on lagged z-scores of `fly`, `slope` (5s10s) and `level`:

| regressor | β (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **butterfly (fly)** | +20.2 | **+1.98** |
| slope (y10 − y5) | +1.7 | +0.25 |
| level (y10) | −8.6 | −0.92 |

The butterfly is **not** merely the 2s10s slope in disguise — the slope control is flatly
insignificant (*t* = +0.25) and the curvature keeps almost all of its loading. But conditioning on
level and slope pulls the butterfly's own *t* down to **+1.98**, back below the bar.

## Quintile spread — Q5 (high fly) − Q1 (low fly) forward IEF return

| horizon | Q5 | Q1 | spread | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d | +13.8 | +1.5 | +12.4 bps | +1.64 |
| 21d | +58.5 | +5.4 | +53.0 bps | +1.66 |
| 63d | +165.5 | +16.0 | +149.5 bps | +1.67 |

The monotone, right-signed spread survives the coarser quintile lens — but the discretised *t*
sits **~1.66**, comfortably below 2. The regression *t* > 2 leans on the tails the quintiles blur.

## The twist (the *change* in curvature)

Forward IEF `~` lagged z(`dfly`): *t* = **+0.65 / −0.38 / +1.56** at 5/21/63d. **Nothing.** A
day-over-day *twist* of the curve carries no forward information here — only the standing *level*
of curvature does.

## Robustness — three eras (the decisive cut), fly → IEF `h=21`

| era | β (bps) | HAC *t* | R² | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **2002-2009** | **+48.7** | **+3.32** | **10.32%** | 1,782 |
| 2010-2017 | −1.8 | −0.18 | 0.02% | 1,927 |
| 2018-2026 | +7.2 | +0.59 | 0.27% | 2,050 |

**This is the study's spine.** The whole full-sample effect lives in **2002-2009** (*t* = +3.32,
R² = 10%) — the pre-crisis/GFC regime — and **evaporates** afterward: it is a coin-flip in
2010-2017 (*t* = −0.18) and in 2018-2026 (*t* = +0.59). The butterfly→belly relation is **not
stable across eras**, which is exactly the bar a `REAL` stamp must clear.

## Placebo — is the full-sample *t* a lucky alignment?

Shuffle the (lagged) butterfly against forward IEF returns, re-fit the HAC regression, 500 times:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed \|t\| | **2.337** |
| permuted *t* mean (sd) | +0.030 (**1.047**) |
| two-sided *p* | **0.024** |

Against an *i.i.d.-shuffled* null the observed *t* is a genuine 2.3σ event (*p* = 0.024). But that
placebo **destroys the regressor's persistence**; the honest null (below) — which *keeps* the
butterfly's autocorrelation — is wider, so this *p* is an **optimistic** floor.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Own IEF when the lagged butterfly rank > 0.5, else cash; one-way cost per switch on the NAV:

| one-way cost | active | passive (buy-hold) | spread/day | *t* | Sharpe (active / passive) | switches/yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +1.02 bps | +1.41 bps | **−0.39 bps** | −0.96 | 0.557 / 0.522 | 13.5 |
| 2 bps | +0.96 | +1.41 | −0.45 | −1.09 | 0.527 / 0.522 | 13.5 |
| 5 bps | +0.80 | +1.41 | −0.61 | −1.49 | 0.439 / 0.522 | 13.5 |

The timer **loses to buy-and-hold on mean return** at every cost (spread −0.39 to −0.61 bps/day).
The wafer-thin Sharpe "edge" at 1 bp (0.557 vs 0.522) is a **volatility artefact** — sitting in
cash on low-curvature days trims variance more than it trims return — and it inverts once realistic
friction bites. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased (and the HAC caveat)

Deterministic seeded tape whose butterfly, rebuilt from a self-consistent 5y/10y/30y yield block,
predicts forward IEF returns only when `fly_signal > 0`. No network.

| world | regression *t* | Q5−Q1 spread *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| planted (`fly_signal = 0.02`) | **+33.99** | +24.70 |
| null (`fly_signal = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean +0.03 (sd **1.37**), \|t\|≥2 in **5/20** | mean +0.00 (sd 1.30), \|t\|≥2 in 5/20 |

The detector recovers a *planted* twist edge overwhelmingly (*t* ≈ +34) and centres on zero under
the null — so the machinery is unbiased. **But the null *t* has sd ≈ 1.3, not 1.0, and clears
\|t\|≥2 in ~5/20 draws:** a persistent regressor against overlapping (MA-structured) forward
returns makes the HAC *t* **over-reject** in finite samples. The real full-sample *t* = 2.34 is
therefore worth roughly **1.8 effective σ**, not 2.3 — one more reason the honest read is *weak,
not real*. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The butterfly (curve *curvature*) does predict forward **belly-Treasury
  (IEF)** returns with the right sign and a full-sample HAC *t* just past 2 (**+2.34** at 21d,
  β = **+16.9 bps/1σ**), and it is *not* just the 2s10s slope repackaged (the slope control is
  insignificant). But it **fails the era-stability bar** the desk requires for `REAL`: the entire
  effect is a **2002-2009** phenomenon (*t* = +3.32, R² = 10%) that is **dead** in 2010-2017
  (*t* = −0.18) and 2018-2026 (*t* = +0.59); the quintile version is sub-2 (*t* = 1.66), the
  incremental *t* falls to 1.98, and the synthetic null shows the HAC *t* is inflated (real *t* ≈
  1.8 effective σ). Right direction, real literature behind it, but this tape cannot certify it.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The curvature timer loses to buy-and-hold on mean return at every cost
  (−0.39 to −0.61 bps/day); its sliver of a Sharpe advantage is a cash-parking volatility artefact
  that inverts under realistic friction.
- **Twist adds beyond level+slope? — MIXED.** The *standing curvature* carries marginal (unstable)
  information the slope does not; the *change* in curvature (`dfly`) carries **none** (*t* ≈ 0).
